A hallmark significant only in the full cohort and lost on sample_01 removal should be reported as depth-sensitive, not as a finding

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq count matrix from Salmon (12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples) with an unpaired 6 lesional vs 6 control design in human skin. The question has two parts — which genes change, and which hallmark pathways change — plus one explicit data concern: sample_01 has a library size roughly 4x below the median.

The plan therefore starts with a QC/normalization step (T1S1) that quantifies the depth outlier rather than assuming it is fatal: library sizes, detected-gene counts, median-of-ratios size factors, VST/rlog PCA, and sample-sample correlation clustering decide whether sample_01 is merely shallow (low depth, but sitting with its condition group in expression space) or a genuine outlier (separating from its group). Median-of-ratios normalization plus the negative-binomial model already absorb a 4x depth difference through the size factor and the dispersion-weighted precision, so exclusion is not the default. The step records the decision and, critically, the group membership of sample_01 — dropping it from a 6v6 design leaves 5v6 and skews power toward one arm.

T1S2 runs the primary differential expression: DESeq2 on raw integer counts, ~condition with control as reference, independent filtering, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, and shrunken log2 fold changes (apeglm) for ranking. The design is unpaired and single batch, so no covariate is warranted; adding one would only burn residual degrees of freedom at n=12. T1S3 is the sensitivity analysis the caveat demands: re-run the identical contrast with sample_01 excluded and quantify concordance against the full-cohort result. If the two gene lists agree, the shallow sample is a non-issue and can be stated as such; if they diverge, the primary result is depth-driven and must be reported with that caveat. This is the only honest way to close the 'handle it carefully' instruction — deciding by inspection alone is not evidence.

T2S1 answers the pathway half using the MSigDB human hallmark collection (50 sets, HGNC symbols) confirmed present in the reference store. It uses fgsea on the full DESeq2 ranked statistic rather than an over-representation test on a thresholded list, because GSEA uses every gene and does not depend on an arbitrary FDR cut — important at n=6 per group where the significant list may be short. Leading-edge genes are reported so the pathway calls stay traceable to the T1S2 gene-level evidence, and hallmark stability is checked against the sample_01-excluded ranking from T1S3. The counts matrix is ~12,000 x 12 and a few MB at most, so every step is small: 2-4 cores and 4-8 GB throughout.
